## Introduction

As new language models and agentic systems are released, the evaluation benchmarks designed to test them are being solved at an unprecedented rate. Rather than asking *if* a model can beat a specific test, the more relevant question in evaluating AI progress is *how fast* that test becomes obsolete. 

In this post, we step back to look at the lifecycle of 36 major cognitive benchmarks. By analyzing the gap between the best AI score on the day a benchmark was published and the current state-of-the-art score, we can visualize the velocity of machine learning advancements and identify which domains are resisting saturation.

## 1.Data Source & Pre-processing

This analysis investigates the cognitive domains where AI exceeds human capabilities using the [AI Benchmarks vs Human Baselines](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/kylefengkfeng209/ai-benchmarks-vs-human-baselines) Kaggle dataset.


```{r}
benchmarks <- read_csv("data/benchmarks.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```
